canal_p14_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_001.text: On the thirty-third morning, the canal smelled of torn leaves and brown clay. Luo's first local reading showed a steady rise that had overtaken the slower change expected before the quarry warning. The ordinary gate stayed out of cargo service. Its operator watched from the protected position while the landing receivers kept boats at higher moorings. Yue carried tea to the observer during her preparation break and felt the cup tremble against its own saucer. Water had begun giving every ordinary sound another meaning.

canal_p14_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_002.text: The temporary house lodging had reached its second offered night. The owner's nephew came to the higher landing and offered two more nights for the two displaced women, with ordinary meals from the household's measured pantry stock. The grandmother accepted after asking whether the children would lose their own beds. They would not. Her son would sleep at his own family's room upriver after taking the actual message there. The finite offer had a source and a time, which made it easier to accept without feeling trapped inside somebody's generosity.

canal_p14_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_003.text: Han's store crew had moved the private surplus hoist and four tagged planks into the high dry room. He wanted one last journey for smaller stock from the lower shed. Luo's current closure barred the low hauling path as its retreat margin narrowed. Han said his own goods still stood above water. The path, not the goods, determined whether people could safely carry them out. He stared toward the shed and named a price Yue could not afford to lose. She listened without letting the price reopen the checked limit.

canal_p14_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_004.text: A private worker asked whether refusal meant Han would replace him after the storm. Han had never spoken that threat, but the old sale notice made every new work call sound larger than its words. He said the closed path ended the task and would pay the actual accepted handling interval already complete. The worker put down his empty rope basket. Yue watched relief come through his shoulders. Han's store still had a lawful owner. Today that owner needed to let a person leave before his goods did.

canal_p14_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_005.text: The smaller stock included a lacquered chest once used by Han's mother. It held household papers and little personal things he had not wanted in the busy upper store. Yue understood the pull of the chest after seeing the grandmother wrap her painted cup. Han asked whether a cultivator could reach it by another way. Yue had no leg route, no flight and no safe private passage beyond the closed path. She told him the actual upper window and dry apron could be assessed by the trained crew if their current interval allowed it, without promising the object a rescue.

canal_p14_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_006.text: Luo asked the road receiver to assess the higher window route for people first, since the store occupied two levels. Han said everybody had left. The clerk asked him to name the completed head count against the actual private work list. One young worker had gone upstairs to cover the flour jars, and nobody had received his return. Han's face changed. The missing person made the window assessment urgent for a reason his mother's chest had not supplied. The road workers were already in their funded ground interval and came from the higher landing.

canal_p14_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_007.text: They called from the stable apron beneath the upper store window. A voice answered after a long moment, angry rather than injured. The young worker had shut the inner door against blowing rain; a shifted crate now blocked it from the other side. His upper room remained above present water, but the lower stair route crossed the closed wet path. Han wanted to push through from the shed. The crew leader kept him on the apron and asked the worker what could move inside his own room.

canal_p14_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_008.text: The flour jars stood too close to the upper window to let him climb out without moving them first. The worker began heaving a full one toward the wall. Its glazed foot slipped on the floor, and he stopped when the crew called. Yue asked whether he could empty a light bag into the smaller dry tub and move only the manageable jar. He checked his actual space and did that. The task cost flour handling damage in Han's private stock, which mattered less than making the opening usable.

canal_p14_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_009.text: The road workers brought their checked ordinary ladder onto the higher apron. Its rating covered one person at a time, and they secured its footing on the sound ground before setting the upper contact. Bao examined the reachable support surface as a carpenter within his current response task. The old window sill held, but a loose decorative cover would not support a hand. He marked the sound frame and removed the loose cover from the dry side. The young worker waited inside instead of reaching for the first thing that looked solid.

canal_p14_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_010.text: Rain blew under the window while Bao worked. He stepped sideways to keep a falling cover fragment off the ladder's base and put one hand out against the wall. His boot slipped on a wet private packing cloth dragged across the apron by wind. He fell to the level paving, catching himself badly on that wrist. The ladder remained secured and unloaded. Yue heard his sharp breath before seeing how he held the hand. The road leader stopped the work long enough to move him clear on ordinary ground.

canal_p14_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_011.text: Bao could stand and walk, but he could not grip without pain. He wanted to finish checking the sill. The crew leader told him his observed support check was already recorded and his injured wrist no longer belonged on the ladder task. Yue brought a dry wrap from the first-aid kit included in the hired gear. The ordinary trained worker supported the hand without trying to set an uncertain injury. Bao cursed at the packing cloth, then at himself for moving faster than his feet could keep.

canal_p14_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_012.text: Han gathered the loose cloth from the apron and put it into his private store. He said it had been tied down earlier, then admitted nobody checked it after the wind changed. The cause could be examined later; Bao needed ordinary care now. Han offered to pay the actual clinic bill from his private current loading receipts, separately from the reserved deposit envelope. Bao accepted that offered payment without signing away any claim. The road crew resumed the person-first window plan with its second worker replacing Bao's physical assistance.

canal_p14_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_013.text: The young worker looked out and asked whether he had hurt the carpenter by getting trapped. Yue said the ladder had not carried him yet, and the apron slip had its own actual circumstances. He did not need to apologize himself into making a faster climb. The crew leader repeated the current steps: move the light obstruction, take the sound marked handhold and descend one person at a time under the ladder's rating. Rain tapped the frame while the man listened from the room he had finally made less crowded.

canal_p14_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_014.text: Jiang stood at the nearby guarded apparatus position, watching its isolated small pocket and present head. The local rain had not pushed that pocket beyond its checked condition, but outside water was approaching the crew's withdrawal mark. She could not power the store ladder or haul a room through Yue's arms. She offered the accepted small release response only if it became necessary to finish isolating the pocket before retreat. The rescue would remain an ordinary ladder task on present sound ground, with a clear ending if that ground changed.

canal_p14_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_015.text: Yue wanted to help everywhere at once: Bao's wrist, the trapped worker, the small mechanism and Han's fear. Luo gave her one current job, reading the apron's retreat mark for the crew while Bao went with a keeper assistant to the ordinary clinic room on higher ground. The assistant's regular public duty covered the escorted walk; no new emergency worker-day appeared. Yue looked at the fixed mark and called the current level. It stayed below withdrawal, giving them a real limited interval rather than a timeless chance to be brave.

canal_p14_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_016.text: The young worker moved the lighter jar clear and found his coat underneath. He wanted to take the coat, then laughed shakily at worrying about wool while everyone watched. The crew leader said he could wear it if doing so did not delay the prepared descent. He put it on and kept both hands free. Han wanted him to bring the small personal chest too. Luo said the current window opening served a person. Han stopped himself halfway through another sentence and called the worker's name instead.

canal_p14_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_017.text: At the ladder foot, the second road worker checked the secured base after the rain changed direction. Its sound apron remained outside the wet path. The crew leader stood beside him, giving the worker clear instructions from below while the ladder carried only its single climber. Yue watched the retreat mark and heard Han begin counting steps under his breath. The young man tested the sound frame and placed one boot on the first rung, then moved his other hand onto the ladder's checked rail.

canal_p14_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_018.text: He froze when the open air below the window became visible. The room had felt safe because the floor surrounded him. The ladder offered a narrower certainty. The crew leader let him pause while Yue called the current ground mark still below withdrawal. She wanted to urge him faster, then remembered the grandmother's actual pace. Fear did not obey a schedule by being scolded. The worker shifted his grip to the marked frame, breathed once and brought his other boot onto the ladder.

canal_p14_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_019.text: The first descending steps held. Halfway down, his coat hem caught a protruding peg beside the window. He tugged instinctively and rocked his balance. The leader told him to stop, keep both feet seated and one hand on the rail, then lift the caught hem with his free hand. Yue kept the ground call steady. Han shut his eyes and opened them when the cloth came free. The coat tore at its edge, losing a little usefulness to preserve the person's much greater ordinary body.

canal_p14_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_020.text: The worker reached the apron and stepped onto sound ground before the retreat mark was met. The crew led him directly to the higher landing rather than pausing for his story under the window. He said his knees felt absurdly weak. The road worker gave him a dry seat in the actual receiving shelter and checked for injury using the ordinary first-aid procedure. He had a scraped knuckle and fright, not a broken limb. Han joined them after securing the now-empty work list, leaving his mother's chest in the lower shed.

canal_p14_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_021.text: The current worker head count matched every person on Han's private handling list. The forgotten upper return had caused a real dangerous delay. Han signed that fact in his own incident note rather than saying the storm made it impossible to count. The rescued worker asked that the missed handover be changed before another private shift. He wanted an actual return acknowledgment from upper rooms, even during ordinary weather. Han agreed. The store could improve its work practice without requiring the young man to call his rescue a debt.

canal_p14_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_022.text: Bao's ordinary clinician found a painful wrist sprain after examining movement and checking for signs that required further referral. He fitted a support, prescribed rest from gripping or loaded work and set a review in several days if pain persisted. He did not promise a sudden healed hand. Han paid the actual one-copper clinic bill from private loading receipts as offered. Bao kept his remaining work rights and unresolved incident account. Yue visited after her current ground interval ended and found him furious about how boring recovery would be.

canal_p14_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_023.text: He said the window would have needed only five more minutes of his hand. Yue asked whether those minutes would have made the wrist improve. He said no, then laughed angrily at the obvious question. She admitted she had wanted to command something merely to feel less useless beside his pain. Bao said the ordinary wrap had been useful. Neither answer comforted him entirely. The sprain would cost real tasks in the next days, and a good conversation could not restore their hours to the timetable.

canal_p14_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_024.text: The emergency receiver reviewed Bao's accepted hours with him before scheduling the next interval. His unused three-quarter day equivalent, six hours, could be reassigned to the two qualified road workers at the same rate if he agreed and the work order authority accepted the change. Bao would receive wages for his actual completed one-and-a-quarter equivalents, not lose earned pay because injured. The receiver recorded the authorized reassignment. The emergency labor still totaled eight equivalents: Yue two, Jiang two, Bao one-and-a-quarter and road workers two-and-three-quarters.

canal_p14_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_025.text: The two road workers accepted three additional hours each for the next response tasks. Their changed ending times remained within the actual available itinerary; they would not be counted awake indefinitely. Bao kept a rest place above the keeper's shed while his private household arranged the next ordinary visit. The original repair schedule would also need to replace his loaded hand tasks before they could resume. Yue watched him sign with his other hand, each letter awkward enough to make the lost grip visible on the work sheet.

canal_p14_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_026.text: By afternoon, the local river run entered the seasonal hollow more strongly. The observed outer spill followed much of the repaired route toward the basin, but brown water began pooling near the clay dip below the house. The household had already left, the reed shelter was empty and the bean rows were unoccupied. Luo received those actual head counts before asking about boards. Prepared empty places could still suffer damage. They did not need bodies standing beside them to make their losses count afterward.

canal_p14_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_027.text: The small upper pocket remained inside its isolation limit, but its draining response now needed completion before the broader station reached withdrawal. Jiang asked Yue whether her own route was recovered for the one accepted sequence, with the ordinary manual fallback ready. Yue said it was. The selector would operate only the small side-release into its checked catch, never hold the flood outside it. The road crew's actual next intervals could also watch the ground path and keep current messages moving while the mechanism finished its last useful task here.

canal_p14_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_028.text: Luo offered Yue three ways to serve the next response. She could take the prepared small control under Jiang, stay with the moving ground observers or help carry the actual closure and missing-return lessons to the higher shelter receivers. The qualified crew would complete the other jobs within their changed finite appointments. Bao would rest his injured wrist. Han would leave his chest behind. Their losses and limits now occupied the same afternoon as the water, and no choice would turn them back into yesterday.

canal_p14_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_029.text: The pocket's actual head stayed inside its rating while the broader station approached withdrawal. Yue could perform the accepted small release, follow the ground observers moving higher or deliver the current closure to people waiting for loved ones and property news. Each path had a real ending before darkness. The young worker sat wrapped in his torn coat, alive on higher ground. Bao sat nearby with his wrist supported. Their ordinary bodies made the difference between finishing a useful task and continuing one simply because somebody had started it.

choices.text: Complete the small release under Jiang's supervision.
Follow the ground observers as they move higher.
Deliver the actual closure to shelter receivers.

canal_p14_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_030.text: Jiang checked the actual catch outlet before accepting the small pocket's response. Its receiving channel still stood below the pocket outlet reference, with a visible clear run into the checked upper return. The broader hollow's rising flow had not yet backed into this small separate path. The independent observer called the pocket head inside rating and the dry station below withdrawal. Yue took her marked place. The task had a real current window, and none of its acceptance depended on imagining the flood smaller than it was.

canal_p14_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_031.text: The quarter-unit command formed along her recovered arm route within the established half-unit delivery allowance. She felt the familiar small warmth and wanted it to mean that the night was manageable. Jiang's call kept the meaning narrower. The selector moved the accepted side-release, and external supply powered its bounded actuator. Yue released at the scheduled point. Water left the little pocket through its actual clear catch while the independent observer watched the fixed head. The flood elsewhere continued rising, unimpressed by the useful small sequence.

canal_p14_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_032.text: A loosened light cover edge fluttered toward the observer sheet while the pocket drained. The road worker caught it from his dry position and tied it away from the guarded moving path. Yue stayed at her release point, fighting the urge to leave the completed command half-finished so she could help with cloth. The observer called the falling pocket mark. Jiang accepted the response and isolated the supply after its planned dry-closing comparison. The cover did not get to choose a second job for Yue's already used route.

canal_p14_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_033.text: The accepted powered sequence had drawn twenty supply units across its response and dry checks. Jiang wrote the actual remainder against the post-inspection gauge that retained the original trial-path difference. The conservative floor fell from two hundred seventy-six to two hundred fifty-six; the precise actual count remained separately recorded. Yue copied the gauge only after her hands settled enough to write. She had used one small command within its earned allowance. It would need recovery before another day could ask for anything similar.

canal_p14_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_034.text: The little pocket was now empty and its side-release returned to the accepted safe state. The outside station's rising margin brought the current withdrawal call soon afterward. Jiang isolated the supply case and the road crew helped carry its protected light components along the ordinary clear retreat. They left the heavy fixed frame in its secured location. Yue walked from the selector with both feet on the marked paving, the route she had rehearsed while the cover still smelled dry. No opened leg pair arrived to make it graceful.

canal_p14_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_035.text: At the higher landing, Yue felt her arm routes ache while the ground still seemed to move beneath her memory of the water. Jiang asked for the ordinary sensation report and gave her the booked rest that followed the accepted sequence. The response had completed its small isolation task before conditions changed. Yue wanted to know whether she had done enough. Jiang said she had done the accepted task and would know more from the current ground reports. Enough for the whole storm was not a quantity her body could provide.

canal_p14_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_036.text: The rescued store worker sat near them mending nothing, staring at his torn coat. Yue offered the clean thread Tian had sold in a small personal kit earlier, but asked whether he wanted a repair now. He said he wanted his hands to stop shaking before using a needle. She put the kit away and brought warm tea from the shelter's actual household pot. He told her the flour jars sounded like rain even after he left the room. Yue said she still heard the actuator after its case was closed.

canal_p14_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_037.text: Han came to thank her and Jiang for completing the little pocket before retreat. Yue pointed him toward the road crew's actual person rescue, which had used a ladder and his worker's own careful steps. He went there next without turning back for another speech. She felt pleased by her command and embarrassed by how much she wanted that pleasure witnessed. Jiang said useful pride could survive beside an accurate account. Yue tried to let it remain a small feeling instead of expanding it into a larger explanation of the night.

canal_p14_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_038.text: Bao asked how the response went from his supported chair. Yue described the actual outlet check, twenty-unit draw and timely withdrawal. He asked whether anybody used his injured hand in the report as if it supplied another shift. She said the receiver had reassigned his remaining hours before the road crew accepted them. He nodded, then asked her to hold his cup while he adjusted its angle with the other hand. The ordinary favor felt awkward only because both of them had spent the day wanting more dramatic forms of usefulness.

canal_p14_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_039.text: At the emergency receiver's desk, Yue delivered her completed sequence and actual recovery status. Jiang's gauge held the precise supply remainder, with twenty additional units used in this response. The isolated little pocket and clear retreat had been observed separately from the rising outer hollow. The person rescue and Bao's wrist incident remained their own accounts. Yue put down the pen and went to the booked rest place without reopening the apparatus merely because the rain made sitting still feel morally difficult.

canal_p14_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_040.text: The ground observers moved from the lower station when the outer flow reached its actual withdrawal mark. Yue followed the road crew along the checked inner retreat, carrying the field sheet while the nearer speaker gave the full move-higher call. The house yard lay beyond brown water, unoccupied. From the next sound mark, they could still see the crossing lip without standing beside it. A larger distance made the view less exact. It was the view they could safely keep, which mattered more than reading every small line.

canal_p14_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_041.text: One observer reported a dark crack beside the outer apron, then corrected himself after seeing a loose reed move through the same line. It might be surface flow at the edge rather than a widening ground break. Yue kept the initial warning and the revised observation together. The crew had already moved higher under the actual water mark. No one returned to the exposed edge to settle whether the crack had been frightening enough. Their next ground position gave another measured source, and the night would have to work with that.

canal_p14_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_042.text: At the higher mark, the road leader checked his ordinary line gear and its planned use around the stable waiting area. The line guided people along the retreat boundary; it would not hold a flood through somebody's waist. Yue remembered the store ladder and asked whether a stranded person could still be reached beyond the wet path. The current head counts showed nobody there. If new evidence changed that, the crew would assess a real rescue from current ground rather than offer a standing invitation to wander into brown water.

canal_p14_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_043.text: Jiang completed the little pocket's accepted response using the ordinary selector control at its protected station. The side actuator drew sixteen actual supply units through the checked current drain and closing sequence; no command from Yue's own routes was required. Its catch still had an observed clear fall into the upper return. The precise gauge count kept the original trial-path remainder. The conservative floor after this branch was two hundred sixty. The crew isolated the emptied pocket and withdrew when the broader station met its actual limit.

canal_p14_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_044.text: Yue received the actual response report at the higher mark and copied it beside the outer route's current observations. The powered task had not controlled the wider flood, which still carried loose clay toward the basin. The inner departure path remained clear for their final return. She called the current footing and watched a discarded private basket turn slowly in the brown run below. Somebody would miss the basket later. Its moving shape did not justify putting a living body where the path had already closed.

canal_p14_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_045.text: The gardener came to the higher landing asking whether his remaining beans had vanished. Yue could see the outer row under scattered shallow water but not every plant. She gave the actual view and its time. He wanted a definite count now. The road leader said the crop inspection would wait for checked lower ground. The man sat on the edge of the dry bench, holding his empty basket. Yue stayed beside him without promising that a better report tomorrow would somehow preserve tonight's unseen leaves.

canal_p14_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_046.text: A small child asked whether the water was allowed to take beans. The gardener said no, then laughed bitterly at the question. Yue said people could record the actual loss and decide a claim, even when water had no person who could be persuaded to stop. The child offered a single bean left in her pocket from market. Her father took it gently and put it into his empty basket. The little kindness did not balance a field. It stopped the bench being only a place where they waited to hear bad news.

canal_p14_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_047.text: The final inner station closed after the next observed rise reduced its footing margin. Yue and the road crew used the actual higher retreat before water reached their boots. The near relay received the closure and went to its own checked position. Behind them, the path's outer edge began carrying a narrow brown stream. Yue wanted to stay one minute longer to remember its exact shape. The crew leader called her name, and she moved. A report could lose a detail without losing the observer who might write the next one.

canal_p14_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_048.text: At the landing, the current head counts included every field observer and the rescued store worker. The house's two displaced women remained at their actual offered room; the reed gatherer stayed in the higher shed. Bao rested with his wrist supported. Yue checked the list through actual return acknowledgments rather than assuming a visible crowd included everyone who left a station. Han read that process over her shoulder and asked for a copy to change his private upper-room handover before his next working day.

canal_p14_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_049.text: Yue delivered the completed ground response and received Jiang's sixteen-unit supply record from the small isolated pocket. The precise actual remainder stayed in the gauge account. Her own route remained unused and recovered in this branch. She had worked through feet, voices and current marks while the qualified operator completed the mechanism. The rain continued outside the receiving shelter. Yue sat where the gardener could find her if he wanted the current view repeated, without pretending she could make that view kinder by describing it a second way.

canal_p14_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_050.text: The higher shelter was full of people asking for news about different kinds of things. Yue carried the current closure in its dry cover and began with actual people accounted for before answering property questions. The grandmother and owner had their real temporary room for two more nights. The reed gatherer had his accepted bed above the hollow. The store worker sat alive with a scraped knuckle. Nobody's goods became unimportant because those statements came first. They simply did not get to stand in place of a missing person.

canal_p14_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_051.text: The grandmother's son asked whether the house was still dry. Yue had the current yard view from the appointed observer, showing pooled brown water outside the threshold. The inside floor had not been inspected. She read that actual report rather than saying it was probably fine. The son clenched his jaw. His mother asked whether the protected higher shelf could still be seen. It could not from the current sound mark. Yue left that question open and offered the next scheduled report instead of inventing a glimpse.

canal_p14_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_052.text: Han wanted his personal chest included in the report. Its lower shed stood beyond the closed path, with no current interior view. Yue recorded its location and ordinary ownership for later retrieval when the ground reopened. He said the papers could dissolve before then. She understood and refused to promise a dry object she had not seen. The rescued worker listened from his seat. Han looked at him and stopped asking for another private expedition into the wet path. His mother's things would have to wait with his own fear.

canal_p14_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_053.text: The garden owner asked about the little private close board. It had been left at its accepted ordinary position before the crossing exceeded its working condition. The field crew had withdrawn rather than forcing it against higher untested head. She wanted to know whether the board still stood. Yue had no current close view. She gave the actual last sighting and its time. The owner read it carefully, then asked for the later receiving inspection. She knew enough about the fitted job to ask a question a future report could answer.

canal_p14_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_054.text: Jiang sent the small-pocket report through the actual road receiver. The protected catch still had a checked falling outlet when she completed the side-response with the ordinary selector. Its powered drain and accepted closing comparison drew eighteen supply units. No command from Yue's body was required in this branch. The conservative floor fell to two hundred fifty-eight, with the precise actual trial-path remainder preserved in the gauge record. The crew then isolated the emptied pocket and withdrew under the broader station's actual ground limit.

canal_p14_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_055.text: Yue read that report at the receiving table and showed Luo the actual completion time. The little mechanism had finished before the station closed. The outer hollow continued carrying water beyond its accepted low-flow behavior. The shelter's people heard the difference in plain words. A working small release could be useful during a storm without solving the storm. Yue felt less frustrated when she saw how much uncertainty remained in the room even after people learned that one particular job had truly ended.

canal_p14_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_056.text: Tian came with the emergency cover invoice already accepted and paid inside its two-copper material line. Her own evening stitching kit stayed in her bag. The store worker asked whether she could mend his torn coat after his hands stopped shaking. She offered an ordinary price for the small repair and a later time if he wanted it. He accepted, relieved that asking did not create a permanent service in either direction. Yue watched the torn wool become a future little appointment instead of another scar the flood had to make symbolic.

canal_p14_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_057.text: Pei brought the public return sheet from the keeper's counter and asked each actual receiver to read the names assigned to that station. The clerk had marked the upper store worker returned only after the road crew confirmed him. Han wanted the same separate acknowledgment in his private future list. The worker approved his own name's use for that practical incident lesson, but declined a public hero story. Pei kept the rescue outcome in the official account without printing his frightened pauses beside it for spectators.

canal_p14_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_058.text: The gardener asked whether every crop loss would be blamed on the seasonal use he had opposed. Yue told him the current account would compare observed route, rain, quarry reports and actual crop inspection after safe return. The old charter did not certify every future cause. He said he did not want to hear a careful explanation if the beans were dead. She said he could be angry and still offer evidence. He sat quietly afterward, leaving the empty basket on the table where a clerk could not mistake it for a completed claim.

canal_p14_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_059.text: At the shelter receiver's desk, Yue delivered the current closure, last property sightings and actual small-pocket report with eighteen additional supply units used. Her own arm route remained unused and recovered in this branch. The people waiting now had specific open questions and their next receiving times. She had carried bad news honestly enough that the room stayed uncomfortable. Outside, the storm made the roof louder than every voice. Yue helped pour ordinary tea and let the next actual observation interrupt supper when it came.

canal_p14_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_060.text: The emergency receiver assembled the three actual response reports in their own signed sequence. The little pocket had been drained, isolated and left before its broader station closed; its precise supply draw followed the path actually taken. The conservative post-response floor was two hundred fifty-six, with higher actual remainders preserved rather than averaged. Every known worker had reached higher ground. Bao's sprained wrist and the missed private upper-room handover remained real incidents. None became harmless because the crew could now read a complete return list.

canal_p14_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_061.text: At dusk, the grandmother set her painted cup on the offered room's low table and asked for news again. The current yard view showed water outside the house, with no safe interior inspection yet. Her son wanted to apologize for leaving on the parcel journey. She said the actual crew brought her out before he returned, which was what their arranged help was for. He sat down. Yue left them tea from their own host's pot and went back to the receiving shelter, relieved that one guilt did not need to be invented.

canal_p14_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_062.text: Han kept his mother's chest location in the retrieval account while paying the rescued worker's accepted private handling wage. The coat repair would be the worker's ordinary small purchase after Tian's appointment, not a deduction imposed because he had been trapped. Han offered to pay that repair too after seeing the torn edge, and the worker accepted without waiving his requested handover change. The current loading receipts covered the small bill separately from the reserved deposit money. A private business could admit a loss without making the person nearest it pay.

canal_p14_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_063.text: Bao slept badly with his wrist supported against a folded blanket. He woke whenever rain struck the shed roof and thought somebody called him back to the gate. Yue sat beside him during her accepted rest overlap, not as an extra paid medical worker. The ordinary clinician's instruction remained rest from gripping and loaded work. Bao wanted a knife to carve a peg one-handed. Yue offered paper for a drawing instead. He complained, then drew a peg so crooked that both of them laughed despite themselves.

canal_p14_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_064.text: Near midnight, the quarry receiver's fresh message reached Luo through the actual timed road relay. More of the stock bank had slumped, and stronger runoff entered the upper branch. The public officer had withdrawn his own exposed crew to checked ground. He reported their actual return and the present direction of water. Luo entered the message and moved the canal's planned observation interval to its next higher position. Yue could see the local rise now. The warning still mattered because it named what had changed before their own mark told the whole story.

canal_p14_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_065.text: The repaired ordinary gate cap stayed seated under the keeper's protected view while the current head remained within its observed service state. The gate was closed to cargo, and nobody treated its earlier successful traffic as flood certification. Bao's original maintenance drawing stayed available to the actual operator. Yue copied the current mark from the sound station without moving closer for a better look. The old cap's groan was gone. Tonight its absence sounded strange, as if danger had lost a familiar voice without becoming quieter.

canal_p14_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_066.text: On the thirty-fourth morning, a broken willow branch drifted into the lower seasonal turn. From the high mark, the road observer could see it catching reeds and slowing the spreader. The house yard began pooling more visibly. The crew did not enter the brown flow to tug a tree by hand. Their actual current report identified an obstruction and the ground from which it could be assessed later. The route had worked under small clean water. This larger water carried objects their original test had never promised to command.

canal_p14_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_067.text: Luo sent the observed obstruction to the public water officer and asked for an actual current assessment of possible clearing from protected ground. The officer's crew had its own standing duty and available equipment, with no instant arrival assumed. The first answer gave a later time and an upstream checked approach. Meanwhile the canal kept people away from the lower hollow and recorded its current marks. Yue wanted action that felt proportionate to the house's wet yard. Waiting on safe ground felt emotionally smaller than its practical value.

canal_p14_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_068.text: The gardener saw his outer rows submerged from the higher landing. He asked Yue to count every drowned bean, then apologized because he knew she could not see them. She said he did not need to apologize for wanting a count. They marked the actually visible flooded area on his offered plot sketch, preserving the crop receipt and earlier harvest dates for later inspection. The remaining private cart journey had saved several baskets. Its useful outcome did not make the unharvested rows a voluntary gift to common water.

canal_p14_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_069.text: The reed gatherer's old shelter bent under the branch-caught reeds. Its sailcloth roof tore at one corner, visible from the high mark. His bed and cutter were already in the higher shed. He wanted to retrieve a small carved spoon he had forgotten. The current closure applied to that object too. Yue helped him record its last known location without promising a recovery. He laughed sadly that he had moved the heavy machine and left the easy thing. Real preparation could work well and still leave someone missing a little piece of home.

canal_p14_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_070.text: Tian accepted the rescued worker's coat repair with Han's offered private payment documented. She patched the torn hem using material the owner had approved from his own small kit, outside the emergency cover purchase. The worker tried it on after his knuckle was cleaned. He said the patch would always remind him of the ladder. Tian asked whether he wanted it on the inside. He did. She changed the stitching so his daily coat could carry a memory without displaying it to everyone he met.

canal_p14_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_071.text: The garden owner wanted to return for her seed parcel receipt after remembering it inside the house. Her son had carried the actual parcel and receiving acknowledgment yesterday; the receipt had already reached the higher family room. She found it under the grandmother's wrapped cup and cried with relief that seemed too large for one sheet. Yue recognized the feeling. Fear could scatter known facts as easily as paper. The people at the shelter helped one another remember where ordinary things had actually gone.

canal_p14_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_072.text: The public water officer arrived by his checked upper approach late in the morning, carrying his own current duty authority and assessment tools. He examined the lower turn from the protected high station and confirmed the branch's present obstruction. Removing it immediately through the rising flow would exceed his crew's safe reach. A controlled clearing might become possible after the head stopped climbing, with a rated line system from actual sound ground. Luo accepted that current finding and kept the people out. The branch would remain an actual cause to examine, not a command everybody failed to shout loudly enough.

canal_p14_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_073.text: Jiang read the protected supply gauge after the completed response, preserving its actual path count and the conservative lower floor. She had remaining accepted emergency hours for another bounded task after current conditions and her appointment allowed it. The lower obstruction did not convert the small side-release frame into a tree-hauling machine. The public officer's rated line work had its own real gear and duty scope. Yue put the two tasks on separate sheets, grateful for an ordinary way to resist imagining that more charge meant every tool could do more work.

canal_p14_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_074.text: Bao wanted to join the officer's branch assessment as soon as he heard it. The supported wrist still hurt at light grip, and the clinician's restriction remained. Luo asked him to review the current timber drawing from his chair instead of handling a line. His original ordinary repair hours reserved for later light checking were not spent by this offered discussion. He chose to make the suggestion as a personal answer, then stopped when tired. Yue saw how difficult it was to keep expertise present without making an injured person prove he still belonged.

canal_p14_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_075.text: By afternoon, the local rise slowed but had not turned downward. The officer would not accept a branch clearing merely from a slower increase. Luo read the actual unchanged high-water state to the shelter receivers. The grandmother's two additional offered nights still had time remaining, and her host had provided the promised ordinary meal. The road crew checked its revised remaining paid intervals before the next response. Nobody could spend the same six transferred hours twice because the storm seemed long enough to deserve more help.

canal_p14_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_076.text: Yue made her ordinary recovery check at the booked rest place and recorded its actual baseline against the sequence she had performed. Her earned arm pairs remained at their second-pair stage. She put away the tile without repeating a reassuring sensation. The next useful task would have to begin with current ground and a specific tool. The storm's size did not make another threshold appear, but neither did it erase the small work she could already do.

canal_p14_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_077.text: Han looked out from the higher landing toward his lower shed. He said his mother would have called him careless for leaving the chest there. Yue asked whether she would have wanted the worker to carry it down the ladder before himself. Han said no after a long pause. He still wanted the chest. The two answers could stand together without making him either noble or monstrous. He went to review the actual private handover change with the worker, choosing one repair he could do today.

canal_p14_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p14_078.text: At dusk, the officer's fixed mark showed its first small fall after the long high interval. He recorded an observed fall, with another check required before lower work resumed. The branch still held reeds across the turn, and the yard remained wet. Luo sent the exact reading and time to the shelter, then called Jiang and the revised road crew to consider tomorrow's bounded work. Yue stood beside the dry apparatus cover with her route recovered. The night they stopped hauling had saved people; the next day would test what could be repaired without risking that result.
